text: In theme generation, the researcher interprets shared meaning across coded data and actively constructs relationships among codes; theme importance is not determined by the number of codes or data items. The article describes reviewing candidates first for coherence among the data items and codes within a theme, then against the dataset and research question. Review can lead to recoding, restructuring, adding or removing sub-themes, or discarding a candidate. In Byrne's example, an initially dense and incoherent candidate theme was broken into three themes after renewed interpretation; this illustrates the procedure rather than a universal expected outcome. (Publisher PDF pp. 1403–1406.)
